cards.text: Friend, Jeremiah the prophet gets another word from the LORD, and this one's about Egypt. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is coming to strike the land of Egypt. And the LORD says don't keep it quiet: announce it in Egypt, in Migdol, in Memphis and in Tahpanhes.

cards.question: The message announced in Migdol, Memphis and Tahpanhes warns that the sword devours those around them. So what does it tell them to do?

answers.text: Take your positions and prepare yourself
Open your gates and welcome the king
Lay down your weapons and rest awhile

cards.text: Then the LORD asks a question. Why have Egypt's warriors been laid low? They can't even STAND.

cards.question: Egypt's warriors can't stand, because the ___ has thrust them down.

cards.text: They keep stumbling, and they fall right over one another. That's every stack of cookie boxes I ever piled TOO high, all going down at once.

cards.question: Egypt's stumbling warriors say to each other, Get up, let's go. True or false: they want to go back to their own people and the land of their birth.

cards.text: And there, they'll cry out about the man in charge: Pharaoh king of Egypt.

cards.question: When the warriors cry out about Pharaoh king of Egypt, what do they say about him?

answers.text: He was all noise and let his time pass
He fought for them to the very end
He sent them help right on time

cards.text: All noise. Like the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, swearing they had charge left and never powering a THING. Then the King speaks, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: The King, the LORD of Hosts, says one is coming who is like Tabor among the mountains. True or false: the LORD swears to it by His own life.

cards.text: So one is coming who is like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea. And Memphis, one of the towns that got the announcement, will be laid waste, destroyed and uninhabited.

cards.question: With Memphis about to be destroyed, the LORD tells the daughter dwelling in Egypt to pack her bags for ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD paints a picture, and Egypt is the star of it. Egypt is a beautiful heifer.

cards.question: Egypt is a beautiful heifer. What does the LORD say is coming against her from the north?

cards.text: A beautiful heifer versus a BUG, and friend, I have personally lost that fight to one fly in my bakery. Even the mercenaries among her are like fattened calves.

cards.question: The day of calamity is coming upon the mercenaries among Egypt, the time of their punishment. True or false: the mercenaries will stand their ground.

cards.text: The enemy will advance in force against Egypt. And Egypt is going to make a sound.

cards.question: As the enemy advances, Egypt will hiss like a fleeing ___.

cards.text: With axes they'll come against her, like woodsmen cutting down trees. They'll chop down her forest, dense though it may be.

cards.question: Egypt's forest is dense, but the enemy chops it down anyway. Why can they?

answers.text: They are more numerous than locusts
They set the whole forest on fire
The trees have already dried out

cards.text: More than locusts, too many to count, and I can't even count the chocolate chips in ONE batch. The Daughter of Egypt will be delivered into the hands of the people of the north.

cards.question: The Daughter of Egypt is handed over to the people of the north. True or false: the LORD says she will be put to shame.

cards.text: Now the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, gets specific. He's about to punish Amon, god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh, and Egypt with her gods and kings.

cards.question: Besides Amon, Pharaoh, and Egypt's gods and kings, the LORD names one more group. True or false: those who trust in Pharaoh will be punished too.

cards.text: He'll deliver them into the hands of those who seek their lives: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But the LORD isn't done talking about Egypt.

cards.question: After Egypt is handed over to Nebuchadnezzar and his officers, what does the LORD say comes next for Egypt?

answers.text: It will be inhabited as in days of old
It will stay empty for all time
It will be covered over by the sea

cards.text: Egypt gets lived in again, and friend, a stamper who got pulled out of a junk drawer does NOT argue with a comeback. Then the LORD turns to Israel, His servant Jacob.

cards.question: The daughter dwelling in Egypt was told to pack her bags. What does the LORD tell Jacob, His servant?

cards.text: The LORD says He will SURELY save Jacob out of a distant place, and Jacob's descendants from the land of their captivity. Friend, distance is no problem for the One who sent for a stamper stuck at the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Once the LORD saves them, Jacob will return to ___ and ___, with no one to make him afraid.

cards.text: Then the LORD says it again to His servant Jacob: do not be afraid. Twice in a row, friend. When God repeats Himself, lean in.

cards.question: The second time the LORD tells Jacob not to be afraid, what reason does He give?

cards.text: The nations where the LORD banished Jacob? He will completely destroy them. Jacob? NOT completely.

cards.question: The LORD won't completely destroy Jacob. True or false: He says He will leave Jacob with no discipline at all.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three separately punctuated sentences or sentence fragments: "All noise.", the battery comparison, and "Then the King speaks...."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question begins, "Once the LORD saves them," but the antecedent of "them" is found only on the preceding story card, which is no longer on screen. The question should identify Jacob and his descendants itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: By saying that the LORD speaks "again" and that the command occurs "Twice in a row," the card uses both Jeremiah 46:27 and Jeremiah 46:28, but it cites only Jeremiah 46:28.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
